subject: FinEx throughput sizing — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amelia Ford <amelia.ford@finex.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinEx throughput sizing — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the call this morning — high level recap and a few clarifications so your sizing team can prepare an initial estimate. Appreciated the walkthrough of Redwood’s streaming behavior and batching knobs.

Quick recap of FinEx production goals we discussed:
- Target 99th percentile latency (end-to-end, for streaming responses) <= 150ms for token chunks after first byte.
- Average tokens per request: median ~120 tokens, 95th ~420 tokens, peak ~800 tokens (large document summarization).
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~75 requests/sec.
- Expected peak burst QPS (minute-level spikes): ~250 requests/sec for up to 10 minutes during market open.
- Concurrent active sessions (long-running streaming connections): ~600 concurrently streaming users at peak.
- Percentage of requests that need streaming (token-by-token): ~65%. The remainder can be non-streaming batch responses.

Primary questions for the sizing workbook:
1) For streaming requests, what per-token throughput and per-token latency assumptions will you use when sizing GPUs?
2) How does Redwood model batching for mixed streaming + non-streaming workloads (e.g., how much latency tail is introduced)?
3) Are there quantized model recommendations we should consider to reduce GPU footprint while preserving quality for our summarization models?

I attached the throughput worksheet we keep internally (finex_throughput_estimates.xlsx) and a simple network diagram. We'll also upload a small sample of production traffic (anonymized) to the Drive folder at the link below.

Request: Could you confirm which model family (open Llama variant vs. your recommended L2-optimized family) your sizing will assume, and whether you can produce a quick Dedicated vs Hosted capacity comparison (cost and latency tradeoffs) by next Wednesday?

Thanks — looking forward to the sizing estimate.

Carlos Vega
Head of Platform Engineering
FinEx Solutions

Attachments: finex_throughput_estimates.xlsx, network_diagram.png
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinEx throughput sizing — post-call recap & next steps

Carlos — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Looping in Marissa (solutions lead) and Neha (performance) to drive the sizing.

We’ll put together an initial workbook that covers:
- Estimated GPUs and pods for: steady-state (75 QPS), sustained high (250 QPS bursts), and peak concurrency (600 streaming connections).
- Per-token latency and throughput assumptions for the model families we discussed (including quantized pathways).
- A cost/latency comparison: Hosted (reserved instance) vs Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for the first 6 months.

A few clarifying items that will materially change the sizing:
- Can you confirm the distribution of request payload sizes? You listed median/95/peak tokens — do you have the percent of requests that are <= 50 tokens, 50-250, 250-800?
- For the 65% streaming requests: are these single-stream responses (one model invocation per user) or long multi-turn interactions that maintain KV cache across messages?
- Do any requests require guaranteed ordered delivery of streamed tokens (i.e., you cannot tolerate out-of-order batches)?

If you can drop the anonymized sample CSV into the Drive link you sent, Neha will run a quick distribution analysis and Marissa will model the initial capacity.

Proposed next steps and timing:
- Today/Tomorrow: FinEx uploads sample traffic (CSV) to Drive.
- Mon 10/5: Redwood returns a draft sizing workbook (GPU counts, expected tokens/sec, QPS, concurrency guidance) + high-level cost delta.
- Wed 10/7: 30-minute follow-up to review assumptions and pick preferred model/quantization profile.

If those dates work, we’ll target the Mon/Wed cadence.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@finex.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinEx throughput sizing — post-call recap & next steps

Adding a couple of quick technical checks from the sizing side:

- Quantization: for summarization workloads with lots of long-context tokens, our recommended starting point is 4-bit QLoRA-like quantization for the Llama-family variants — this typically reduces GPU memory by ~40% with modest impact to quality. We'll model both FP16 and 4-bit in the workbook.
- Batching/streaming interaction: in mixed workloads we size for the streaming fraction first (since streaming is latency-sensitive) and then allocate remaining capacity to batch jobs. In practice you should expect some batching tail — Neha, can you add an example latency tail estimate for 75 vs 250 QPS?

Also: Carlos, if you can share a small sample (first 24 hours or a 1,000-request slice) there's a good chance we can produce a tighter GPU count rather than conservative overprovisioning. Drive link would be perfect.

I'll pencil in Wed 10/7 for the quick review — 10:00-10:30 PT works on our side, but open to other slots.

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinEx throughput sizing — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks — I've uploaded an anonymized 1,000-request sample and a short hourly distribution CSV to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c3FinExSamples

Quick answers to Rafael's clarifying questions:
- Payload distribution (approx): <=50 tokens: 28%, 50-250: 52%, 250-800: 20%.
- Streaming requests are primarily single-response streams per user (no long multi-turn sessions that maintain large KV cache) — occasional follow-ups but not the majority.
- Ordered delivery: important for some market-alert streams (about 10% of streaming volume) but tolerable to use sequence numbers if your service batches internally.

Timeline: we're aiming to finalize capacity recommendations and decide on a pilot by 10/15. Stakeholders: Amelia Ford (CTO), myself (Head of Platform), plus procurement (Procure@finex.com). Please reference deal FEX-2026-042 in any cost docs.

Carlos
